packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-09 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (first reader)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE STATEMENT
- Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of the work or author. I do not name one.
- Beyond the stated rules: the script in most tiles lies obliquely (photographs taken into an opened spine). I made rotated/cropped working copies of image-002, 003, 004, 005, 007, 008, 009, 010 in a private scratch directory (rotation, cropping, one enlargement; no other processing) and read from those and from the originals. I opened nothing else.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)
Two different photographs/views, each with its own overview:

VIEW 1 = image-001 (overview) with tiles image-002, 003, 004, 005. Looking into the spine of a bound volume under a lifted limp cover; ruler at lower left. Manuscript waste lines the spine in panels between thread-wrapped sewing supports:
  (a) CENTRAL PANEL, between two supports: one text block, at least 14 lines, written lines running obliquely up to the right in the photograph. Small, rounded, light-brown, heavily abbreviated script. A red-and-blue pen flourish or paragraph mark sits at the upper-left corner of the panel (image-002). The left margin is visible (a ruled vertical line); the right ends of the lines curl up under the cover fold and are lost. Many abbreviated references of the form ". C . i . q . v ." occur: OBSERVATION. That these are citations by numbered division and question is a TENTATIVE interpretation.
  (b) LOWER-LEFT STRIP (image-004), a separate piece turned about 60 degrees: 15 short lines, darker and larger script, three passages underlined in red, surface abraded in the middle. Both edges cut.
  (c) FAR PANEL (image-001 upper left, behind the central panel): c. 12 lines of a larger, black script, entirely out of focus - unread.
  (d) NEAR-RIGHT PANEL (image-005, lower right of image-001): c. 10 oblique lines plus a strip at lower left, a red paragraph mark at its corner; out of focus.
VIEW 2 = image-006 (overview) with tiles image-007, 008, 009, 010. The head of the volume, colour scale and ruler at left; the endband with loose tie-down threads crosses the lower part.
  (e) MAIN PANEL: one column fragment, 13-14 lines, upright, in a rounder, more widely spaced brown script than (a). Left margin visible; right ends run under the cover fold. Several short phrases are underlined in red; they open with a capital and stand at the start of a sense unit. TENTATIVE interpretation: underlined lemmata followed by explanation.
  (f) LEFT FOLDED STRIP (image-009): 15 short lines running obliquely, both ends cut; similar script to (e); small red touches on two letters.
- No running title, rubric heading or large initial visible in either view. The tight, oblique crops do not show page layout or number of columns.
- Panel (d) in image-005 may be the same parchment as panel (e)/(f) seen from the other side of the volume (the lower-left strip in image-005 begins with letters resembling the first line of the strip in image-009). This is a guess from blurred shapes.

LINE NUMBERING
Lines are numbered from the top of the visible text block in the named image (in VIEW 1 the "top" line is the one nearest the upper sewing support). | = line runs out of view or is cut. (..) = proposed expansion; ? = uncertain.

SPANS SELECTED: (a) all 14 lines; (b) all 15 lines; (e) all lines; (f) all lines. UNREAD: (c) and (d) (focus), right-hand ends of (a) and (e).

(a) CENTRAL PANEL - left parts from image-002, right parts from image-003 (same lines; the two tiles overlap in the middle of each line)
image-002 L1 : g[... under the support ...] p(er)sonas . Aut eciam p(er)[..]|
image-002 L2 : ut i(n) ve..ia? [..]soluere? . h(oc)? d(icitu)r? aut d[..]|
image-002 L3 : tollat(ur) . Vt . i(n) . C . i . q . v? . s(ed)? . t(ame)n? q[..]|
image-002 L4 : que pl(ur)a? ..o? fiant a . e . ep(iscop)o? . t(ame)n? q(ue)? inhib[..]|
image-002 L5 : ert(ur)? . Vt . i(n) . e(odem)? . C . vii . q . ii? . C . h(oc) aut(em) [..]|
image-002 L6 : (et) i(n) . C . i . q . v(l)t(ima)? . tali . Sic (et) i(n) plerisq(ue)? [..]|
image-002 L7 : spensatione(m) mouent . s(cilicet) . ut i(n) secta? ma[..]|
image-002 L8 : Pragmatica . q(ue) fiunt in aug(ust)a? . (et) cet(er)a[..]|
image-002 L9 : sus . (et) p(ro)cessus consistorio . l(icet)? ob causa(m)?[..]|
image-002 L10: nuato? . Quietas? simplex i(n) nex[..]|
image-002 L11: Principis . (et) i(n)d(e)? su(n)t? sacra? mul[..]|
image-002 L12: tam p(ra)g(matica)? a . (et) confirmatis? . un(de)?[..]|
image-002 L13: ..dill..? tria q(ue) imp(er)antis? . s(cilicet) . ad pena(m)?[..]|
image-002 L14: [..]cta q(ue) (con)tra(ri)e? [..] . imp(er)at..? [..]|
  Line ends visible only in image-003 (curled, foreshortened), from top: ..p(er)..| ..d(e) ..| ..ma..| ..aut(em)? v..| ..ple..| ..ecta ma..| ..(et) cet(er)a ..| ..ob causa(m)? ..| ..nex..| ..possu(n)t? ..| ..penis? ..| ..[illegible].
  Secure: "personas . Aut eciam"; "tollatur . Vt in"; the chains ". C . i . q ." and ". C . vii . q ."; "[di]spensationem mouent"; "Pragmatica . que fiunt"; "et processus consistorio"; "simplex"; "Principis".
  (L7 begins "spensatione(m)": the first syllable stood at the end of L6, out of view.)

(b) LOWER-LEFT STRIP - image-004 (both ends of every line cut)
image-004 L1 : |[..]enuenatio? . te[..]|
image-004 L2 : |(et) i(n) . C . xvi . q . v? . [..]|
image-004 L3 : |is . in scriptis . sed? [..]|   (red underline beneath)
image-004 L4 : |W..? s(cilicet)? ita (con)q(ue)st(us)? [..]|
image-004 L5 : |[abraded] ..u.. ..i.. sum?|
image-004 L6 : |..eat(ur)? . v(e)l ex quo s(er)u[..]|
image-004 L7 : |miss(us)? . Cur? sup(er)st[..]|   (red underline beneath the first word)
image-004 L8 : |p(er) pat(ri)moniu(m)? . accu[..]|
image-004 L9 : |n . s..d.. [abraded] ..n..|   (red underline beneath)
image-004 L10: |in . xii . ing(re)ss(us)? t[..]|
image-004 L11: |. Cano(n)e(m)? eciam d[..]|
image-004 L12: |misit possessio(n)e(m)? [..]|
image-004 L13: |ducit(ur)? post bela?[..]|
image-004 L14: |meu(m) . (et) matrem [..]|
image-004 L15: |n mense? secu(n)d[..]|
  Secure: "in scriptis"; ". C . xvi . q ."; "vel ex quo"; "possessio-"; "post"; "meum . et matrem".

(e) MAIN PANEL, VIEW 2 - left parts image-007, right parts image-008, lower lines image-010 (image-009 repeats the left ends of L5-L7; overlaps, not new text)
image-007 L1 : d(icu)nt(ur) qui publice negocia s(e)c(u)l(ar)i? exigu(n)t . l[..]|
image-007 L2 : na sectant(ur) . In eu(an)g(e)lio aut(em) . qui publice p[..]|
image-007 L3 : publicani appellantur . Om(n)ia plenitudo i[..]|      ("Omnia plenitudo" underlined in red)
image-007 L4 : .i. nullus . p(ate)r? . (et) apparere . p(er)fectus in in[..]|
image-007 L5 : n(ost)ram ip(s)e h(abe)t ..? in(iu)stam? faciat . Morte luis . c[..]|      ("Morte luis" underlined in red; a rust-coloured blot covers two letters after "habet")
image-007 L6 : q(ui) i(n) mal(e)dixit pat(r)i v(e)l mat(r)i morte mo[riatur? - end under fold] ob[..]|
image-007 L7 : le(n)ite(m)? infrenat . iactantia(m) cor[..]|      (red underline beneath the first half of the line)
image-010 L8 : [under threads] ..[p(ro)]venientib(us) . S(an)c(t)ificate? [..]|      (red underline beneath the following words)
image-010 L9 : [..]t.. [..]q..[..] sp(irit)uales? [..]|
image-010 L10: sp(irit)u(a)l(ite)r? iudicat . libera[..] ..fab..? g[..]|
image-010 L11: [..] d(e)? uolu(n)tate . s(cilicet) . su[..]|
image-010 L12: [..]e q(ui) iudicat(ur)? . q(ui)a ..[..]|
image-010 L13: [..] p(ro)p(ter)? ..ete[..]|
image-010 L14: [..] . ne[..] (last visible line above the endband)
  Secure: "qui publice negocia"; "sectantur . In eu(an)g(e)lio autem . qui publice"; "publicani appellantur"; "Omnia plenitudo"; ". i . nullus"; "et apparere . perfectus"; "faciat . Morte luis"; "dixit patri vel matri morte"; "infrenat . iactantiam".
  In L6 the scribe wrote "q(ui) i mal dixit" with a stroke over "mal"; I give "maledixit" as an expansion, not as read letters.

(f) LEFT FOLDED STRIP, VIEW 2 - image-009 (top two lines also at the left of image-007); both ends cut
image-009 L1 : |..ellius? . v(e)l sine le[..]|
image-009 L2 : |.. p(e)cc(at)o(rum)? . i(n)tellig[..]|
image-009 L3 : |..uis qua(n)tu(m) ad? [..]|
image-009 L4 : |.. e(st) infamis . i(n)i[..]|
image-009 L5 : |..ustim? moriens p(ro)s[..]|
image-009 L6 : |e(st) . mortale pec[catum?]|
image-009 L7 : |..spicere? . adhuc s[..]|
image-009 L8 : |.. xp(istu)s? . co(n)uenit? il[..]|
image-009 L9 : |..imat(ur)? . na(m) e(st) eni(m)? [..]|
image-009 L10: |..ab(us)? . h(oc) aut(em) sum[..]|
image-009 L11: |..ellit(ur)? . Ab(?) ma[..]|
image-009 L12: |.. [s]ed? . nationes [..]|
image-009 L13: |..is . v(e)l [..]|   (crossed by a paste ridge)
image-009 L14: |..mo(n)ta..? . N[..]|
image-009 L15: |..ntatus? . (et) i(n) s[..]|
  Secure: "vel sine"; "quantum"; "est infamis"; "moriens"; "mortale pec-"; "adhuc"; "nationes".

LIMITATIONS / REQUESTS
- All readings in (a) and (b) are taken from oblique, foreshortened photographs; letter proportions are distorted and minim groups are unsafe. The right-hand third of every line of (a) is effectively lost in these images.
- (c) and (d) are out of focus in every supplied tile and remain unread; (d) shows a red paragraph mark and red underlining like (e).
- Whether (a), (b), (e)/(f) come from one manuscript cannot be decided: (a) is a smaller, more cursive-looking hand; (b), (e), (f) are larger bookhands and (b) and (e) share red underlining. These are observations of appearance only.
- Requested: focused, square-on images of each lining panel (especially (c) and (d)), and a view showing the right-hand ends of (a) and (e).
- Unverified image reading; no gaps were filled from sense or from any edition.
